content.value_statement: WooCommerce backend changes need consistent PHP patterns, hooks, data integrity, and tests. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Explains WooCommerce backend file and class placement conventions.
Guides method, variable, parameter, and hook naming choices.
Describes PHPDoc, PHPStan, and @since annotation expectations.
Shows data integrity checks for CRUD and deletion operations.
Provides WooCommerce unit test structure and fake logger guidance.
Covers dependency injection patterns for internal services.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not run tests automatically.
It does not replace a WooCommerce maintainer review.
It assumes the target project follows current WooCommerce trunk conventions.
It focuses on backend PHP, not storefront design or JavaScript builds.

use_cases.title: Implement backend features
use_cases.description: Create or change WooCommerce PHP classes while following namespace, file, hook, and docblock rules.

use_cases.title: Review data operations
use_cases.description: Check deletion, modification, and batch logic for ownership, state, capability, and race condition safeguards.

use_cases.title: Prepare unit tests
use_cases.description: Plan PHP unit tests with clear fixtures, assertions, test names, and WooCommerce-specific test helpers.

prompt_templates.title: Start a backend change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the WooCommerce backend development skill. Help me plan a small PHP backend change and list the conventions I must follow.

prompt_templates.title: Add a service class
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a new internal WooCommerce service class. Include file placement, namespace, constructor or init method, and docblock requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review data integrity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my WooCommerce data modification flow. Focus on authorization, ownership, entity state, race conditions, and return value handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan tests and hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill before writing PHP unit tests. Plan tests for a backend change that adds a hook, updates a service, and modifies order data.

output_examples.input: Plan a new WooCommerce order processing service.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering internal class placement, dependency injection, method naming, @since handling, hook documentation, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Review a draft order deletion flow.
output_examples.output: A review that highlights status checks, ownership checks, capability checks, race condition risks, and safer soft delete options.

output_examples.input: Prepare unit tests for a backend logger change.
output_examples.output: A test outline with fixture setup, readable test names, assertion messages, fake logger behavior, and cleanup expectations.

best_practices: Invoke the skill before changing backend PHP or writing unit tests.
Provide the target WooCommerce area, files, and expected behavior.
Ask for data integrity and hook documentation checks before final review.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for frontend styling or merchant-facing copy work.
Do not skip project tests or maintainer review after using it.
Do not treat illustrative examples as complete production implementations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants follow WooCommerce backend PHP conventions for classes, hooks, data operations, annotations, and tests.

faq.question: Does it write production-ready code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance that still needs local testing and human review.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include WooCommerce unit test guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers test structure, naming, assertions, fixtures, fake loggers, and cleanup practices.

faq.question: Does it handle data integrity concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. It prompts checks for entity state, ownership, capabilities, race conditions, and safe deletion behavior.

faq.question: Is it useful outside WooCommerce?
faq.answer: Only partly. Most guidance is specific to WooCommerce and WordPress backend PHP conventions.
